body_text: View All News Mettler-Toledo International Inc. to Host Second Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call July 6, 2026 COLUMBUS, Ohio--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Mettler-Toledo International Inc. (NYSE: MTD) announced it will release its second quarter 2026 financial results after the market close on Thursday, July 30, 2026. The Company will host a conference call the following morning at 7:30 a.m. Eastern Time to discuss the results. To listen to the live audio webcast of the call, visit Events and Presentations on the Investor section of the Company’s website, investor.mt.com . METTLER TOLEDO (NYSE: MTD) is a leading global supplier of precision instruments and services. We have strong leadership positions in all of our businesses and believe we hold global number-one market positions in most of them. We are recognized as an innovation leader and our solutions are critical in key R&D, quality control, and manufacturing processes for customers in a wide range of industries including life sciences, food, and chemicals. Our sales and service network is one of the most extensive in the industry. Our products are sold in more than 140 countries and we have a direct presence in approximately 40 countries. With proven growth strategies and a focus on execution, we have achieved a long-term track record of strong financial performance. For more information, please visit www.mt.com . title: Where 5 of YC's Biggest Companies Had Their First Offices | Tandem
summary: Airbnb, Stripe, Coinbase, DoorDash, and Reddit started on air mattresses and in dorm rooms. See where, and what, their offices look like now.
body_text: Share: Where Five of YC's Most Valuable Companies Actually Started BS Brendan Suh Brendan is a licensed real estate salesperson and has helped hundreds of growing startups find their office space. Published Jul 7, 2026 | Updated Aug 6, 2026 Airbnb. Stripe. Coinbase. DoorDash. Reddit. Combined, they're worth more than $500 billion. Today they lease over a million square feet of office space between them — some of the largest commercial real estate deals in the Bay Area. Not one of them started in an office. They started on air mattresses, in dorm room sublets, in live-work lofts where founders slept on the floor because there was nowhere else to put a bed. Here's exactly where — and what happened when the apartment stopped working. Airbnb's First Office Was a 3 Bedroom Apartment in SoMa Where it started: 19 Rausch Street, San Francisco In September 2007, Joe Gebbia's landlord raised the rent. Both roommates moved out. Brian Chesky drove up from LA to split the apartment with him — and the two were staring down $1,150 in rent with only $1,000 in the bank. Their solution: three air mattresses, a website called AirBed & Breakfast, and three conference-goers paying $80 a night. That apartment stayed Airbnb's headquarters for three years. At its peak, 15 people worked out of the living room daily. By 2010, there was so little space left that Chesky moved out and lived in Airbnb listings for months — he simply didn't have a desk to come back to. Where it is now: 888 Brannan Street, a few blocks from the original apartment. The 2012 lease on ~170,000 sq ft ran up to $97 million over 10 years. In October 2024, after shopping the market, Airbnb renewed 250,000 sq ft through 2037. Somewhere inside is an exact replica of the Rausch Street living room — rebuilt as a conference room. Reddit Was Built in Three Weeks in a Medford Sublet Where it started: A furnished sublet in Medford, Massachusetts Steve Huffman and Alexis Ohanian found the place on Craigslist in June 2005. Their entire starting capital was a $12,000 check from Y Combinator's very first batch. Huffman built Reddit in three weeks flat. Their housemate — a Harvard physics PhD student who kept getting woken up by server crashes — taught himself to restart them. He's Reddit's CTO today. Where it is now: One full floor (47,872 sq ft) of 303 Second Street, at a starting base rent of $3.35 million a year. Stripe Started in a Palo Alto Cottage Where it started: A tiny cottage off Ramona Street, Palo Alto Stripe launched on a $20,000 YC check. Co-founder Greg Brockman has said the cottage was packed so tight he had to "climb over people" just to reach his desk — and it's still his favorite office the company has had. Where it is now: Two headquarters. The US base is ~421,000 sq ft on the South San Francisco waterfront, a 12-year lease signed in 2019 estimated at $27.5 million a year. Every Stripe office since has been built around a central staircase — a deliberate design choice meant to force teams to run into each other. Coinbase Started in a Live-Work Loft in SoMa Where it started: A shared two-bedroom live-work loft at 1 Bluxome Street Coinbase launched in October 2012, splitting the space with another startup to cut costs. Bitcoin was trading around $6. There was no boardroom, so the Series A pitch happened in space borrowed from LendingClub. Bitcoin meetups were hosted right in the apartment. Where it is now: Coinbase became famous for having no office at all — its S-1 literally listed headquarters as "Address Not Applicable," and in 2023 it paid $25 million just to exit its San Francisco lease. In 2025, it came back: 150,000 sq ft in Mission Rock, San Francisco, plus an 11-year lease at One Madison Avenue in New York. DoorDash Was Built in the Stanford Dorms Where it started: Stanford dorm rooms, as PaloAltoDelivery.com The founders built the landing page in an hour, put their own cell numbers at the bottom, and delivered the first order — pad thai — themselves. After YC, the team crammed 15 people into a two-bedroom Palo Alto apartment. Tony Xu slept on an air mattress, and when a new hire showed up for her first day, he rolled it up so the place would look more legitimate. Where it is now: 193,000 sq ft at 303 Second Street — the same building as Reddit — running just above $16 million a year. The Pattern Every one of these companies hit the exact same moment: too many people crammed in a space that isn't meant to be an office. That moment always arrives faster than founders expect. And the traditional way to find office space — built for corporations doing 5-year strategic planning, not startups moving at startup speed — makes it worse. That's the gap Tandem fills. We're an AI-native office brokerage built to help startups lease space at startup speed, compressing the search and cutting out the headache. When your apartment stops working, let us search for you . We'll lead your search At no cost to you, our expert leasing team will help you go from exploring options to moving in. title: AI SRE update: Your feedback shaped our latest release
summary: The latest Mezmo AI SRE update adds streaming progress, log aggregation, and visualization tools to make observability faster and more intuitive.
body_text: A note from Lauren Nagel, Mezmo's VP of Product: At Mezmo, we believe the best observability tools aren't just built for users, they're built with them. Since the launch of Mezmo's AI SRE agent, we've listened and learned from our customers. The feedback and insights have been invaluable in helping our teams refine and enhance the experience. Today, we're excited to share our latest release, packed with improvements and powerful new capabilities that make our AI SRE even faster and more intuitive. What's New in This Release Enhanced User Experience: Inline prompt and query scope guidance for large queries to help you craft more effective requests Streaming progress updates so you can follow along as the AI works through your query Direct links back to error logs for transparency - gotta have those receipts! Ability to cancel requests giving you full control over long-running operations Better performance across the board for faster insights Powerful new capabilities and prompts: Aggregate and summarize logs by field values to quickly understand patterns in your data What are my top apps? What is the sum of _mezmo_line_size for my top apps? Show the min, max, avg, and p99 of _mezmo_line_size for my top apps Find all apps with errors over the last 24 hours Visualize log patterns over time to identify trends and anomalies at a glance Help me identify spikes in log throughput over the last 24 hours Look for spikes in errors for app nginx over the last 12 hours Visualize the average duration for app redis in hourly buckets over the last 24 hours Discover available fields for searching and filtering, making it easier to explore your logs Which fields can I search that contain 'size'? Show all my number fields Get log counts for queries to understand the scope of issues How many logs exist for query: app:nginx level:error? Retrieve surrounding context for a specific log line to see the full picture Analyze the lines surrounding a specific log line These updates reflect our commitment to making AI-driven observability both powerful and practical for your daily workflows. Want access? Simply contact josh.leger@mezmo.com or sign up for a demo request and we'll prioritize your account! Keep the Feedback Coming Your input drives our roadmap. As you explore these new features, we'd love to hear what's working well and where we can continue to improve. This is just the beginning of our journey to transform observability with AI. ‍ ‍

body_text: Back to All A cada mês, evoluímos nossos conectores e SDKs para que você tenha mais confiabilidade, velocidade e precisão nas integrações financeiras. 🚀 Em agosto, avançamos em pontos estratégicos como redução de falhas em fluxos de criação, melhoria de performance em dados de pagamento e ajustes que trazem mais consistência aos conectores. title: The 2026 Burrito Price Index: A State by State Look at Burrito Prices in America
summary: Per Diem helps merchants grow with powerful mobile app solutions integrated seamlessly with Square.
body_text: After releasing the Latte Price Index earlier this year, we continued examining how everyday food prices vary across the United States. This time we turned to another staple of the American fast casual menu: the burrito. The 2026 Burrito Price Index analyzes average burrito prices across 21 U.S. states to understand how the cost of a common meal changes by location. Based on publicly listed restaurant menu prices, the analysis finds that the national average price of a burrito now sits at $12.73. While most states fall within a relatively tight range between $12 and $14, a few markets stand out. New York and Florida rank among the most expensive, while Texas remains one of the most affordable burrito markets in the dataset. Regional differences are influenced by several factors including ingredient costs, rent, labor, and overall dining trends within each market. Even for a menu item as familiar as a burrito, these local conditions can lead to noticeable price variation across the country. The Burrito Price Index offers a simple snapshot of how everyday menu prices shift from one region to another, highlighting how local economics shape the cost of even the most familiar meals. ‍

title: SOLAI Limited Announces Extraordinary General Meeting
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- SOLAI Limited (NYSE: SLAI) ("SOLAI" or the "Company") (previously known as "BIT Mining Limited"), a technology-driven personal AI and digital...
body_text: AKRON, Ohio , July 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- SOLAI Limited (NYSE: SLAI ) ("SOLAI" or the "Company") (previously known as "BIT Mining Limited"), a technology-driven personal AI and digital infrastructure provider, today announced that it will hold its extraordinary general meeting of shareholders at 428 South Seiberling Street, Akron, Ohio, US on August 14, 2026 at 10:00 a.m., New York time. Holders of record of ordinary shares and preference shares of the Company at the close of business on July 20, 2026, New York time (the "Record Date") are entitled to receive notice of, and to attend and vote at, the extraordinary general meeting or any adjournment thereof. Holders of the Company's American Depositary Shares ("ADSs") who wish to exercise their voting rights for the underlying ordinary shares must act through the depositary of the Company's ADS program, Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas. The notice of the extraordinary general meeting, which sets forth the resolutions to be submitted to shareholder approval at the extraordinary general meeting is available on the Investor Relations section of the Company's website at https://ir.solai.com . About SOLAI Limited SOLAI Limited (previously known as "BIT Mining Limited") (NYSE: SLAI ) (previously traded under "BTCM") is a technology-driven personal AI and digital infrastructure provider. Building upon its historical legacy in digital asset mining and blockchain network operations, the Company is leveraging extensive experience in large-scale hardware deployment, data center operations, and high-performance computing to build the foundational infrastructure for personal AI computing and digital asset ecosystems globally.
